item.title: Prof Prasad's trial begins today
item.description: The trial of former Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad begins today at the Suva Magistrates Court. FICAC alleges that on or about 30th December 2015, Professor Prasad failed to declare his directorship in Platinum Hotels & Resorts PTE Limited in his declaration of assets, liabilities and income submitted to the Registrar of Political Parties, allegedly breaching the Political Parties Act
item.content:encoded:
The trial of former Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad begins today at the Suva Magistrates Court.

FICAC alleges that on or about 30th December 2015, Professor Prasad failed to declare his directorship in Platinum Hotels & Resorts PTE Limited in his declaration of assets, liabilities and income submitted to the Registrar of Political Parties, allegedly breaching the Political Parties Act.

He is also charged with providing false information in a statutory declaration, with FICAC claiming that the omission of the directorship made the declaration materially false.

The trial is scheduled to run until Friday.

Richard Naidu is representing Professor Prasad, while Joseph Work is the FICAC lawyer.

FICAC is expected to call four witnesses and rely on six documentary exhibits.

item.title: Family of 10 left homeless after fire destroys Tacirua home
item.description: A family of 10 has been left homeless after a fire destroyed their three-bedroom house in Tacirua, opposite the Fijian School, last night. The National Fire Authority says they received an emergency call at 9.21pm and immediately dispatched firefighters from the Valelevu and Suva fire stations.
item.content:encoded:
A family of 10 has been left homeless after a fire destroyed their three-bedroom house in Tacirua, opposite the Fijian School, last night.

The National Fire Authority says they received an emergency call at 9.21pm and immediately dispatched firefighters from the Valelevu and Suva fire stations.

When firefighters arrived, the timber and corrugated iron house was fully engulfed in flames. Crews managed to bring the fire under control and prevented it from spreading to nearby homes.

The house suffered between 80 and 100 percent damage and was not insured.

Preliminary investigations indicate the fire started in one of the bedrooms, although the exact cause remains under investigation.

National Fire Authority Chief Executive Officer Puamau Sowane says no one was injured in the fire and expressed sympathy to the family as they come to terms with the loss of their home.

He is reminding the public to take simple fire safety precautions, including switching off electrical appliances after use, avoiding overloading power outlets and ensuring electrical wiring is carried out only by licensed electricians.

The National Fire Authority's investigation into the cause of the fire is continuing.

item.title: Children with disabilities continue to face barriers to healthcare, education and essential services
item.description: Many children with disabilities in Fiji continue to face daily challenges accessing healthcare, education and essential support services, with many families struggling to cope because of the high cost of living, limited transport and a lack of specialised care. The Baseline Study of the Rights of Children with Disabilities in Fiji Summary Report highlights that support services remain uneven acros
item.content:encoded:
Many children with disabilities in Fiji continue to face daily challenges accessing healthcare, education and essential support services, with many families struggling to cope because of the high cost of living, limited transport and a lack of specialised care.

The Baseline Study of the Rights of Children with Disabilities in Fiji Summary Report highlights that support services remain uneven across the country, particularly for families living in rural and maritime areas, where access to healthcare, therapy and other specialised services is often limited.

The study found that many children also face barriers in their everyday lives because public buildings, schools and transport are not fully accessible.

It says some Government offices remain upstairs without ramps or lifts, while some schools and communities still lack accessible toilets. The report also found that some taxi drivers have refused to transport children using wheelchairs or were unable to accommodate them.

Families also told researchers that the monthly disability allowance is not enough to meet their needs, with many using the money to cover basic household expenses instead of disability-related equipment and support.

The report highlights delays in accessing assistance because of lengthy application processes, the lack of formal diagnoses and limited awareness of the services available.

It also says wheelchairs and other assistive devices remain in short supply and are often too expensive, forcing many families to rely on donations because there is no dedicated Government budget for these items.

The study is calling for greater investment in disability services, improved accessibility, better transport and stronger support for families to ensure children with disabilities have equal opportunities to learn, access essential services and fully participate in their communities.

item.title: Vanua Levu students can now pursue agriculture careers closer to home
item.description: Soil Science Technician Iosefo Tuisiga is encouraging students to take advantage of the opportunity, saying they can now receive quality training closer to home instead of travelling to Viti Levu. item.content:encoded:
Soil Science Technician Iosefo Tuisiga is encouraging students to take advantage of the opportunity, saying they can now receive quality training closer to home instead of travelling to Viti Levu.

Originally from Vuya in Bua, Tuisiga says the new Living Laboratory Vuvale Garden provides students with practical experience in integrated farming by combining agriculture, animal science, forestry and fisheries in one learning environment.

He says the initiative is designed to equip students with the knowledge and practical skills needed for careers in Fiji's agriculture sector.

Tuisiga is encouraging school leavers and anyone interested in agriculture to enrol in the certificate and diploma programmes offered at the Labasa campus.

He says the programmes provide a valuable pathway into the industry while allowing students to remain in Vanua Levu.

item.title: COVID-19 challenges inspire Vintika to turn candle-making passion into small business
item.description: When the COVID-19 pandemic brought financial uncertainty to many families, Vintika decided to turn her passion for candle-making into a way of supporting her household. Two years later, that decision has grown into a small business producing handmade scented candles for home décor, gifts, weddings and birthdays.
item.content:encoded:
When the COVID-19 pandemic brought financial uncertainty to many families, Vintika decided to turn her passion for candle-making into a way of supporting her household.

Two years later, that decision has grown into a small business producing handmade scented candles for home décor, gifts, weddings and birthdays.

Vintika says she wanted to create something different that was not widely available in Fiji while giving people the opportunity to buy locally made scented candles.

She says building the business has not been easy, with most of the materials needed to make the candles having to be imported because they are not available locally.

Vintika says import duties and the cost of bringing in supplies make it difficult for small businesses to keep their products affordable.

She is calling on the Government to consider reducing import duties on materials used by small businesses, to help local entrepreneurs grow and make their products more affordable for customers.

Vintika credits her family and friends for helping her along the way, saying their support through social media promotion, word of mouth and assistance during market days has been key to growing the business.

item.title: From prison officer to farmer, Fabiano follows his rugby dream home
item.description: The 35-year-old from Vuna Village in Taveuni, with maternal links to Bouma, resigned from the Fiji Corrections Service after nine years before spending nine months overseas, where he worked and played rugby. He returned to Taveuni in 2023 to begin a new chapter as a full-time farmer while continuing his rugby journey.
item.content:encoded:
The 35-year-old from Vuna Village in Taveuni, with maternal links to Bouma, resigned from the Fiji Corrections Service after nine years before spending nine months overseas, where he worked and played rugby.

He returned to Taveuni in 2023 to begin a new chapter as a full-time farmer while continuing his rugby journey.

Rogovakacali's rugby career began with Nadroga in 2011 before he went on to represent the Wardens team during his time with the Fiji Corrections Service.

He later played for Lautoka and Namosi, building years of experience at the provincial level .

Now back on his home island, Rogovakacali spends his mornings working on the farm before preparing for afternoon training sessions, balancing the demands of village life with his passion for rugby.

He says the change in lifestyle has not always been easy, but returning home has allowed him to stay close to his family while continuing to play the sport he loves.

Although he has featured in the Skipper Cup with other unions over the past six years, Rogovakacali says representing Taveuni means more than any previous campaign because he is now playing for his home island.

He says being part of the team is a source of pride , especially after witnessing the hard work and sacrifices made by the players and the wider community to reach this stage.

Rogovakacali thanked his wife, daughter and family for standing by him throughout every step of his journey.

He says he would never have come this far without their love, encouragement and sacrifices, adding that they continue to inspire him to give his best both on and off the field.

Taveuni came close to victory last week when they took on the defending Skipper Cup champions, Malolo, at Lawaqa Park, with Malolo winning 24-23.

item.title: Catholics to honour 182 years of faith in Fiji at historic Lakeba celebrations
item.description: Catholics from across Fiji and overseas will gather in Lakeba next week to honour 182 years since the arrival of the first Catholic missionaries and celebrate a faith that has been passed down through generations. The celebrations on 15th August will also mark the anniversary of the first Catholic Mass celebrated on Fijian soil at Namuka-i-Lau in 1844.
item.content:encoded:
Catholics from across Fiji and overseas will gather in Lakeba next week to honour 182 years since the arrival of the first Catholic missionaries and celebrate a faith that has been passed down through generations.

The celebrations on 15th August will also mark the anniversary of the first Catholic Mass celebrated on Fijian soil at Namuka-i-Lau in 1844.

Diocesan seminarian Brother Fred Kado says Archbishop Peter Loy Chong will bless and unveil a commemorative plaque and memorial stones to honour the arrival of the first missionaries to Lakeba.

Kado says the anniversary is an opportunity for Catholics to reflect on their history while strengthening their faith for future generations.

As part of the lead-up to the celebrations, the Archbishop's Lau Renewal Team has been visiting villages across Lakeba, sharing the history of the Catholic Church in Lau, encouraging community participation and inspiring young people to learn more about their faith.

Kado is inviting Catholics in Fiji and abroad to take part in the celebrations, saying the gathering is a chance to honour the legacy of those who first brought the Catholic faith to Fiji while celebrating the vibrant Church it has become today.
